question_text: A projectile thrown at an angle $30^\circ$ with horizontal from level ground reaches to maximum height $20\text{ m}$. What will be the maximum height if it is thrown at an angle $60^\circ$ with same speed?
solution:
The maximum height attained by a projectile is given by:
$$H = \frac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}$$
For the first throw with $\theta_1 = 30^\circ$:
$$H_1 = \frac{u^2 \sin^2 30^\circ}{2g} = \frac{u^2}{2g} \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{u^2}{8g} = 20\text{ m}$$
This gives:
$$\frac{u^2}{2g} = 4 \times 20 = 80\text{ m}$$
For the second throw with $\theta_2 = 60^\circ$:
$$H_2 = \frac{u^2 \sin^2 60^\circ}{2g} = \frac{u^2}{2g} \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{3}{4} \left(\frac{u^2}{2g}\right)$$
Substituting the value of $\frac{u^2}{2g}$:
$$H_2 = \frac{3}{4} \times 80\text{ m} = 60\text{ m}$$
Hence, the correct option is (4).

question_text: A body is moving in uniform circular motion with speed $v$. The magnitude of change in its velocity after it rotates by an angle $120^\circ$ is
solution:
In uniform circular motion, the magnitude of the velocity remains constant, i.e., $|\vec{v}_1| = |\vec{v}_2| = v$.
The angle between the initial velocity vector $\vec{v}_1$ and final velocity vector $\vec{v}_2$ after the body rotates by an angle $\theta$ is $\theta$.
The magnitude of change in velocity is given by:
$$|\Delta \vec{v}| = 2v \sin\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)$$
Given $\theta = 120^\circ$:
$$|\Delta \vec{v}| = 2v \sin\left(\frac{120^\circ}{2}\right) = 2v \sin(60^\circ) = 2v \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \sqrt{3}v$$
Hence, the correct option is (2).

question_text: A car moves on a circular path such that its speed is given by $v = Kt$, where $K = \text{constant}$ and $t$ is time, the radius of circular path is $r$, then net acceleration of the car at time $t$ is
solution:
The speed of the car is $v = Kt$.
1. Tangential acceleration ($a_t$):
$$a_t = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}(Kt) = K$$
2. Radial (centripetal) acceleration ($a_c$):
$$a_c = \frac{v^2}{r} = \frac{(Kt)^2}{r} = \frac{K^2 t^2}{r}$$
Since tangential and radial accelerations are mutually perpendicular, the net acceleration $a$ is:
$$a = \sqrt{a_t^2 + a_c^2} = \sqrt{K^2 + \left(\frac{K^2 t^2}{r}\right)^2}$$
Hence, the correct option is (1).

question_text: An object of mass $10\text{ kg}$ is projected from level ground with speed $40\text{ m/s}$ at angle $30^\circ$ with horizontal. The rate of change of momentum of object [in SI units] $1\text{ second}$ after the projection is [neglect air resistance]
solution:
According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, the rate of change of momentum of a body equals the net external force acting on it:
$$\frac{d\vec{p}}{dt} = \vec{F}_{\text{net}}$$
For a projectile in flight (neglecting air resistance), the only force acting on it is the force of gravity, directed vertically downwards:
$$\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = m\vec{g}$$
First, checking the total time of flight:
$$T = \frac{2u \sin\theta}{g} = \frac{2 \times 40 \times \sin 30^\circ}{10} = \frac{2 \times 40 \times 0.5}{10} = 4\text{ s}$$
At $t = 1\text{ s}$, the projectile is in flight.
Thus, the magnitude of the rate of change of momentum is:
$$\left|\frac{d\vec{p}}{dt}\right| = mg = 10\text{ kg} \times 10\text{ m/s}^2 = 100\text{ N} \text{ (or } \text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}^2\text{)}$$
Hence, the correct option is (1).
